sources.fact: Be First provides statutory planning services on behalf of Barking and Dagenham and the council directs users to search/comment on planning applications.
Application number or site address is required for comments; the Public Access website is the place to check the final decision and case comments.
Planning registers are a permanent record of planning decisions and planning history, with online publication subject to redaction rules.
LBBD provides an enforcement register and tells users to check whether planning permission has already been granted before reporting a breach.
Applicants may appeal imposed conditions to the Secretary of State via the Planning Inspectorate; an appeal can reopen the whole application.
Planning applications require the relevant validation criteria and are submitted through the planning application process.
LBBD describes validation and written-decision handling; invalid submissions can result from incorrect fees, plans, forms or drawings.
LBBD publishes current validation checklists including a February 2026 Full Planning Applications checklist.
Planning applications are assessed using the Development Plan, including London Plan 2021 and the adopted Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037.
Local Land Charges searches identify restrictions/legal obligations and use information from planning, building control, highways and other bodies; a site plan is required for accurate search extent.
CIL and Section 106 contributions are secured to fund/mitigate infrastructure and development impacts; generic policy does not establish a specific site's obligations.
Larger/significant applications may be decided by Planning Committee; committee involvement is a decision route, not an outcome.

examples.result: Candidate names are never fuzzy-matched to a planning case; exact application reference or exact site address binding is required.
Public Access final decision is treated as case evidence only after the exact reference/site is verified.
A planning comment, committee listing or consultation does not prove permission.
An enforcement-register entry is distinct from refusal, revocation or current development status.
Validation of an application does not mean permission was granted.
CIL/S106 policy does not prove a site-specific contribution unless the actual agreement/notice is bound to the case.
Local Land Charges search scope requires the exact site plan; a nearby charge is not assigned to the candidate.
No planning-status promotion occurs without exact application/site binding and current decision/condition evidence.
